question.text: In the Polson Limited case, what mechanism was used by the company to achieve compliance with the minimum public shareholding requirement?

answer.text: Offer for sale mechanism by selling promoter shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Polson informed SEBI that it fulfilled the minimum public shareholding requirement by selling 11,200 promoter-owned equity shares using the Offer for Sale (OFS) mechanism. The Trap: Rights or bonus issues affect capital structure but may not change the promoter-versus-public shareholding split required for MPS; OFS directly dilutes promoter holding. Note: Anchor the Polson case to the OFS route used to sell 11,200 promoter-owned equity shares for MPS compliance.
